description: How the cost of an operation grows with the input size `n`, ignoring constants. It predicts what happens when data grows, not how fast code is today.
A linear call (`find`, `includes`, `indexOf`, `filter`) inside another loop. The most common performance bug in generated backend code.
An operation that is occasionally expensive (a resize) but constant on average over many calls, like `array.push` or `map.set`.
How memory grows with `n`. Loading a whole file or table is `O(n)` space; streaming or paginating keeps it constant.
A collection whose size has a known small limit (roles, currencies, feature flags). Complexity rarely matters for it.
One query per item inside a loop. Network round trips cost far more than in-memory work, so they dominate the real cost.
